To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of forest as safety net by poor agricultural households is likely to increase deforestation; 2) the diversification strategy is more efficient than the coping strategy; and 3) the use of a safety net is more likely to be implemented in the case of a large increase in the risk aversion coefficient.

(i) agricultural expansion and forest products as safety net are deforestation drivers; (ii) the diversification strategy reduces deforestation more than the coping strategy; and (iii) the impact of forest products on deforestation depends on the forest profitability and on the safety-net strategy.
